turns.doctor_question: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?
turns.patient_response:
Yeah, nice to meet you too. Um, basically, I'm here because things got a bit out of control recently. 

I work in landscaping, and I went from just being a normal crew guy to... well, suddenly I was trying to run three different bids all at once. I was calling city people, lining up plant suppliers, and just messaging everybody I knew about this big park idea I had. I just kept going and going, like I couldn't shut it off.

symptom_reasoning.S040: The patient describes a sudden, massive increase in work-related goal-directed activities, such as running multiple bids, contacting city officials and suppliers, and messaging everyone about a project, stating they 'couldn't shut it off'.

top_partial.disease_name: Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

turns.doctor_question: During this time, were you hearing voices or seeing things that other people couldn’t?
turns.patient_response: No, um, nothing like that. I wasn't hearing voices or seeing anything that wasn't there. It was really just... just my own thoughts, you know? Just me getting way too carried away with all those ideas. But no, no voices or anything.

turns.doctor_question: During that time, did you need much less sleep than usual?
turns.patient_response: Um, no, not really. I think I was sleeping about the same as I usually do. I'd still crash at night and wake up for work the next day. I didn't really notice needing less sleep or skipping it or anything, if that's what you mean. Just... normal sleep, mostly.

symptom_reasoning.S036: The patient explicitly denies needing less sleep, stating they slept about the same as usual.

turns.doctor_question: Were you hospitalized because of this period?
turns.patient_response: No, um, I wasn't in the hospital. I didn't have to go or anything like that. I just... I just kind of burned myself out doing all those bids and talking to everyone, but no, I never got admitted anywhere.

turns.doctor_question: During that period, did your behavior cause serious problems at work or in your relationships?
turns.patient_response: No, um, it didn't cause any serious problems. I still showed up to my landscaping job every day and got all the work done. My boss didn't complain or anything. And things with my family and friends were fine, too. It was really just me being super focused on all those extra projects, but it didn't ruin anything or get me in trouble.

turns.doctor_question: During that time, did you feel unusually confident or powerful, like you could do things other people probably couldn’t?
turns.patient_response: Yeah, I did. I honestly believed I was about to become the main guy every town around here called for sustainable landscaping. Like I was going to take over all of it. Even though, realistically, I’m still just trying to keep my regular small jobs paid up. But at the time, I just felt like I could easily take on a huge level of work like that and succeed.

symptom_reasoning.S035: The patient confirms feeling unusually confident and describes a grandiose belief that they would take over all sustainable landscaping in the area, despite their current reality.

turns.doctor_question: During that time, were you much more irritable than usual?
turns.patient_response: Yeah, I was. Before I crashed, I just felt really fired up... almost bigger than myself, I guess. But because of that, if a coworker questioned my plan or told me I needed to slow down, I'd just snap at him. I reacted way harder than made sense for the situation. So yeah, I was definitely a lot more irritable if people pushed back on what I was doing.

symptom_reasoning.S035: The patient describes feeling 'almost bigger than myself' and reacting poorly to having their plans questioned, indicating grandiosity or inflated self-esteem.
